sourceDate.text: 受業於子夏之倫，為王者師

units.zh: 卷一百上 敘傳第七十上
units.en: Hanshu, volume 100a: the afterword and family history, first installment.
units.literal: Volume 100, Part A: Afterword and Biographical Preface, Number 70, Part A

units.zh: 班氏之先，與楚同姓，令尹子文之後也。
units.en: The Ban lineage traced its kinship to the house of Chu and claimed descent from the chief minister known as Ziwen.
units.literal: The Bans' ancestors shared the same clan name as Chu and were descended from Chief Minister Ziwen.

units.zh: 子文初生，棄於瞢中，而虎乳之。
units.en: Newborn Ziwen was abandoned in the wilderness, where a tigress nursed him and spared his life.
units.literal: When Ziwen was first born, he was cast away in the wilds, and a tiger suckled him.

units.zh: 楚人謂乳「穀」，謂虎「於檡」，故名穀於檡，字子文。
units.en: In Chu speech a mother's milk was "gu" and a tiger was "yutu"; from those words came his personal name, and he received the courtesy name Ziwen.
units.literal: The people of Chu called suckling "gu" and called the tiger "yutu"; therefore he was named Gu Yutu and given the courtesy name Ziwen.

units.zh: 楚人謂虎「班」，其子以為號。
units.en: Chu folk also called a tiger "ban," and his posterity adopted that syllable as their surname.
units.literal: The people of Chu called the tiger "ban," and his descendants used it as their clan designation.

units.zh: 秦之滅楚，遷晉、代之間，因氏焉。
units.en: After Qin conquered Chu, the family was resettled along the Jin–Dai frontier and took "Ban" as their hereditary name.
units.literal: When Qin destroyed Chu, they were moved to the region between Jin and Dai and thereupon took it as their surname.

units.zh: 始皇之末，班壹避墬於樓煩，致馬牛羊數千群。
units.en: Near the close of the Qin First Emperor's reign, Ban Yi escaped unrest by settling in Loufan, where he built up herds counted in the thousands.
units.literal: At the end of the First Emperor of Qin, Ban Yi fled turmoil to Loufan and raised herds of horses, cattle, and sheep numbering in the thousands.

units.zh: 值漢初定，與民無禁，當孝惠、高后時，以財雄邊，出入弋獵，旌旗鼓吹，年百餘歲，以壽終，故北方多以「壹」為字者。
units.en: It happened when Han had only just been settled and there were no restraints on the people. During the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, he dominated the frontier by his wealth; when he went out hawking and hunting, he used banners, flags, drums, and pipes. He lived more than a hundred years and died of old age, so many northerners used the character "Yi" in their names.
units.literal: It happened that the Han had just been pacified and there were no restraints on the people. In the reigns of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, by his wealth he dominated the frontier; he went out and in hawking and hunting with banners, flags, drums, and pipes; he lived more than a hundred years and ended his life in old age; therefore in the north many took the character "Yi" for their courtesy names.

units.zh: 壹生孺。
units.en: Ban Yi was the father of Ban Ru.
units.literal: Yi begat Ru.

units.zh: 孺為任俠，州郡歌之。
units.en: Ban Ru lived the life of a roaming knight-errant, and songs of his deeds spread through the provinces.
units.literal: Ru practiced knight-errantry, and the commanderies sang his praises.

units.zh: 孺生長，官至上谷守。
units.en: Ru's son Chang attained the post of governor of Shanggu.
units.literal: Ru begat Chang, who rose to the office of governor of Shanggu.

units.zh: 長生回，以茂材為長子令。
units.en: Chang's son Hui entered office as magistrate of Changzi on a nomination for outstanding talent.
units.literal: Chang begat Hui, who by nomination as an outstanding talent became magistrate of Changzi.

units.zh: 回生況，舉孝廉為郎，積功勞，至上河農都尉，大司農奏課連最，入為左曹越騎校尉。
units.en: Hui's son Kuang began as a gentleman-attendant after a filial-and-incorrupt recommendation, then climbed by steady service to Capital Agriculture commandant at Shanghe; year after year the Minister of Finance ranked his performance at the top, and he was brought to the capital as colonel of the Yueqi cavalry on the left.
units.literal: Hui begat Kuang, who was recommended as filial and incorrupt and became a gentleman-attendant; through accumulated merit he rose to Capital Agriculture commandant for the Shanghe region; the Minister of Finance reported his annual assessments as repeatedly the highest, and he entered court as colonel of the Yueqi cavalry on the left staff.

units.zh: 成帝之初，女為婕妤，致仕就第，貲累千金，徙昌陵。
units.en: Early in Cheng's reign Kuang's daughter entered the harem as an honored lady; he resigned and went home, amassed wealth reckoned in thousands of gold, and was relocated to the new Changling site.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Cheng's reign, his daughter became an honored lady; he retired to his mansion, his property mounted to a thousand pounds of gold, and he was moved to the Changling project.

units.zh: 昌陵後罷，大臣名家皆占數于長安。
units.en: When the Changling mausoleum town was scrapped, leading families of the court all took out household registration in Chang'an.
units.literal: After Changling was later abandoned, great ministers and eminent houses all registered their residence in Chang'an.

units.zh: 況生三子：伯、斿、稚。
units.en: Ban Kuang fathered three sons named Bo, You, and Zhi.
units.literal: Kuang had three sons: Bo, You, and Zhi.

units.zh: 伯少受《詩》於師丹。
units.en: Ban Bo studied the Odes under Shi Dan while he was still young.
units.literal: In youth Bo received instruction in the Book of Odes from Shi Dan.

units.zh: 大將軍王鳳薦伯宜勸學，召見宴昵殿，容貌甚麗，誦說有法，拜為中常侍。
units.en: Wang Feng urged the throne to employ Ban Bo as a scholar who could inspire study; summoned to the private audience hall, Ban Bo cut a striking figure and lectured with crisp order, and the emperor named him Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Grand General Wang Feng recommended Bo as a man fit to encourage learning; he was summoned to an audience in the intimate banquet hall; his appearance was very handsome, and when he recited and expounded he had a clear method, so he was appointed Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 時上方鄉學，鄭寬中、張禹朝夕入說尚書、論語於金華殿中，詔伯受焉。
units.en: Cheng was bent on scholarship, so Zheng Kuanzhong and Zhang Yu lectured each day on the Documents and the Analects in the Jinhua Palace while Ban Bo was told to join the class.
units.literal: At that time the sovereign was devoted to learning: Zheng Kuanzhong and Zhang Yu came morning and evening to expound the Documents and the Analects in the Jinhua Palace, and the emperor ordered Bo to study under them.

units.zh: 既通大義，又講異同於許商，遷奉車都尉。
units.en: Once he had the larger outlines, he argued fine points with Xu Shang and was promoted to Privy Coachman.
units.literal: After he had mastered the general meaning, he also debated points of agreement and disagreement with Xu Shang, and was promoted to Privy Coachman.

units.zh: 數年，金華之業絕，出與王、許子弟為群，在於綺襦紈褲之間，非其好也。
units.en: When the Jinhua tutorials stopped, Ban Bo drifted into the set of Wang and Xu heirs, a crowd of brocade-clad idlers that never suited him.
units.literal: After some years the instruction at Jinhua came to an end, and he went out to mingle with the sons of the Wang and Xu houses; he moved among youths in silken finery, which was not to his taste.

units.zh: 家本北邊，志節忼慨，數求使匈奴。
units.en: Raised on the northern marches, he burned with blunt ardor and repeatedly asked to be sent on embassies to the steppe.
units.literal: His family's roots lay on the northern frontier; his aspirations were high and forthright, and several times he sought missions to the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 河平中，單于來朝，上使伯持節迎於塞下。
units.en: During the Heping reign the Chanyu visited the capital, and the emperor dispatched Ban Bo with an imperial staff to greet him just inside the frontier.
units.literal: In the Heping years the Chanyu came to court, and the sovereign sent Bo with a staff of authority to welcome him below the passes.

units.zh: 會定襄大姓石、李群輩報怨，殺追捕吏，伯上狀，因自請願試守期月。
units.en: Just then magnate families named Shi and Li in Dingxiang, feuding bloodily, had murdered pursuing constables; Ban Bo filed a report and volunteered to govern the commandery provisionally for one month.
units.literal: It chanced that powerful clans surnamed Shi and Li in Dingxiang, in a chain of private vengeance, had slain the officers sent to pursue them; Bo memorialized on the affair and on his own asked to be allowed to try governing as acting prefect for one month.

units.zh: 上遣侍中中郎將王舜馳傳代伯護單于，并奉璽書印綬，即拜伯為定襄太守。
units.en: The court therefore sent Wang Shun galloping with the imperial insignia to relieve Ban Bo of the reception duty and invest him on the spot as governor of Dingxiang.
units.literal: The sovereign sent Wang Shun, Palace Attendant and General of the Gentlemen of the Household, galloping by relay to replace Bo in escorting the Chanyu. Wang also bore the imperial edict, seal, and cord that appointed Bo Administrator of Dingxiang on the spot.

units.zh: 定襄聞伯素貴，年少，自請治劇，畏其下車作威，吏民竦息。
units.en: The commandery knew Ban Bo as young, noble-born, and hungry for a tough post, and everyone braced for a harsh new governor who would swagger in with threats.
units.literal: Dingxiang had heard that Bo was by nature a man of high rank and was still young; he had of his own accord asked for a difficult jurisdiction, so they feared that when he stepped down from his carriage he would throw his weight about—officials and commoners held their breath.

units.zh: 伯至，請問耆老父祖故人有舊恩者，迎延滿堂，日為供具，執子孫禮。
units.en: Instead he sought out venerable locals and long-standing friends of his forebears, filled his hall with guests, fed them daily, and treated them with the deference of a grandson.
units.literal: When Bo arrived, he called on the elders and on old friends of his father and grandfather toward whom he bore past kindness, welcomed them until the hall was full, each day spread feasts for them, and observed the courtesies due from a grandson.

units.zh: 郡中益弛。
units.en: Tension in the commandery eased further.
units.literal: The commandery became still more relaxed.

units.zh: 諸所賓禮皆名豪，懷恩醉酒，共諫伯宜頗攝錄盜賊，具言本謀亡匿處。
units.en: The notables he had wined were local titans who, warmed by his courtesy, drank deep and urged him to tighten the dragnet and map every hideout of the feuding clans.
units.literal: Those whom he had honored and feasted were all celebrated leaders of opinion; moved by kindness they grew drunk and together remonstrated with Bo that he ought to take firm hold of registering bandits and plainly state where the original conspirators had fled and hidden.

units.zh: 伯曰：「是所望於父師矣。」
units.en: Ban Bo answered, "That is exactly the counsel I wanted from elders I respect."
units.literal: Bo said, "That is what I hoped to hear from fathers and teachers."

units.zh: 乃召屬縣長吏，選精進掾史，分部收捕，及它隱伏，旬日盡得。
units.en: He then assembled county heads, picked sharp subordinates, fanned them out in teams, and within ten days every fugitive and accomplice was in custody.
units.literal: He thereupon summoned the chief clerks of the subordinate counties, selected able clerks and aides, and sent them out in detachments to round up all of them, along with other hidden culprits; within ten days he had the whole lot.

units.zh: 郡中震栗，咸稱神明。
units.en: The whole commandery stood in awe and hailed him as uncannily effective.
units.literal: The commandery trembled with awe and all called him inspired.

units.zh: 歲餘，上徵伯。
units.en: A little over a year later the emperor recalled Ban Bo to court.
units.literal: After more than a year the sovereign summoned Bo back.

units.zh: 伯上書願過故郡上父祖冢。
units.en: Ban Bo asked leave to detour through Dingxiang and tend the graves of his father and grandfather.
units.literal: Bo submitted a memorial asking permission to pass through his former command and visit the tombs of his father and grandfather.

units.zh: 有詔，太守都尉以下會。
units.en: An edict ordered the sitting governor, the commandant of dependent states, and every official beneath them to gather with him.
units.literal: An edict was issued that the governor and the commandant of dependent states and all ranks below should assemble.

units.zh: 因召宗族，各以親疏加恩施，散數百金。
units.en: He called his clan, graded gifts by kinship nearness, and handed out several hundred pounds of gold.
units.literal: He then called together his kinsmen and, according to closeness of kinship, showed them favors and scattered several hundred pounds of gold.

units.zh: 北州以為榮，長老紀焉。
units.en: Northerners spoke of the scene with pride, and old men still recounted it.
units.literal: The northern region considered it glorious, and the elders recorded the deed.

units.zh: 道病中風，既至，以侍中光祿大夫養病，賞賜甚厚，數年未能起。
units.en: A stroke struck him en route; once home he held titular rank as Palace Attendant and Grand Counselor of the Household under lavish stipends, yet for years he could not leave his bed.
units.literal: He fell ill on the road with a wind stroke; when he arrived he was allowed to convalesce as Palace Attendant and Grand Counselor of the Household, with rich gifts, but for several years he could not rise.

units.zh: 會許皇后廢，班婕妤供養東宮，進侍者李平為婕妤，而趙飛燕為皇后，伯遂稱篤。
units.en: After Empress Xu fell, Lady Ban withdrew to serve the Dowager in the eastern palace, a maid named Li Ping rose to an honored lady, and Zhao Feiyan took the empress's seal; Ban Bo promptly claimed serious illness.
units.literal: When Empress Xu was deposed, Lady Ban waited upon the eastern palace; a waiting woman named Li Ping was promoted to honored lady and Zhao Feiyan became empress; Bo thereupon pleaded grave illness.

units.zh: 久之，上出過臨候伯，伯惶恐，起視事。
units.en: Months later Cheng called on him while touring nearby estates; terrified of seeming disloyal, Ban Bo roused himself and went back on duty.
units.literal: After a long time the sovereign, on an outing, stopped by to inquire after Bo; Bo was frightened and bestirred himself to take up office.

units.zh: 自大將軍薨後，富平、定陵侯張放、淳于長等始愛幸，出為微行，行則同輿執轡；
units.en: Once Wang Feng was gone, favorites such as Marquis Zhang Fang of Fuping and Marquis Chunyu Chang of Dingling won the emperor's intimacy: on town trips they slipped out in disguise, and on the road they shared his chariot and took the reins.
units.literal: After the grand general died, Marquis Zhang Fang of Fuping, Marquis Chunyu Chang of Dingling, and others first came to enjoy imperial favor: when they went abroad they joined incognito excursions, and when they traveled they rode the same carriage and held the reins;

units.zh: 入侍禁中，設宴飲之會，及趙、李諸侍中皆引滿舉白，談笑大噱。
units.en: Inside the palace they threw banquets where the Zhao and Li women and the gentlemen-attendants tipped their cups, bellowed toasts, and roared with laughter.
units.literal: when they entered to attend in the inner palace they held drinking parties at which Zhao, Li, and the gentlemen-attendants drained their cups and shouted "Dry!" and talked and laughed with loud guffaws.

units.zh: 時乘輿幄坐張畫屏風，畫紂醉踞妲己作長夜之樂。
units.en: Beside the imperial couch stood painted screens of King Zhou drunk and draped over Daji in the revels of the endless night.
units.literal: At the time the imperial carriage had a draped seat and hanging painted screens showing King Zhou drunk and sprawling on Daji as they indulged in the pleasures of the long night.

units.zh: 上以伯新起，數目禮之，因顧指畫而問伯：「紂為無道，至於是虖？」
units.en: Noting that Ban Bo had lately returned to favor, the emperor kept glancing at him politely, then jerked his chin at the scene and asked Ban Bo, "Was wicked King Zhou really as bad as this?"
units.literal: Because Bo had recently risen, the emperor repeatedly glanced at him with courtesy and, pointing at the painting with his chin, asked Bo, "Zhou was utterly wicked—did it really reach this point?

units.zh: 伯對曰：「書云『乃用婦人之言』，何有踞肆於朝？
units.en: Ban Bo replied, "The Documents says, 'Then he used women's words'—how could there have been such sprawling license at court?
units.literal: Bo replied, "The Documents says 'then he used women's words'—how could there have been such sprawling license at court?

units.zh: 所謂眾惡歸之，不如是之甚者也。」
units.en: What people call 'every evil was ascribed to him' means the truth was not in fact this extreme."
units.literal: What is called "every evil was ascribed to him" means it was not in truth this extreme."

units.zh: 上曰：「苟不若此，此圖何戒？」
units.en: The emperor said, "If it was not like this, what warning does this picture carry?"
units.literal: The emperor said, "If it was not like this, what warning does this picture carry?

units.zh: 伯曰：「『沈湎于酒』，微子所以告去也；
units.en: Ban Bo said, "'Sunk deep in drink' is why the viscount of Wei announced his departure;
units.literal: Bo said, "'Sunk deep in drink' is why the viscount of Wei announced his departure;

units.zh: 『式號式謼』，大雅所以流連也。
units.en: 'Shouting this way and roaring that way' is why the Greater Odes linger on it with sorrow.
units.literal: 'Shouting this way and roaring that way' is why the great odes linger on it with sorrow.

units.zh: 詩書淫亂之戒，其原皆在於酒。」
units.en: The warnings in the Odes and Documents against licentious disorder all trace their source to wine."
units.literal: The warnings of the Book of Odes and the Documents against licentious disorder all trace their source to wine."

units.zh: 上乃謂然歎曰：「吾久不見班生，今日復聞讜言！」
units.en: The emperor thereupon sighed as if agreeing and said, "I have not seen Ban for a long time; today I have again heard blunt straight speech!"
units.literal: The emperor thereupon sighed as if agreeing and said, "I have not seen Ban for a long time; today I have again heard blunt straight speech!

units.zh: 放等不懌，稍自引起更衣，因罷出。
units.en: Zhang Fang and his set scowled, excused themselves to change robes, and drifted out until the party collapsed.
units.literal: Fang and the others were displeased, rose one after another on the excuse of changing clothes, and therefore left the gathering.

units.zh: 時長信庭林表適使來，聞見之。
units.en: An agent from the Changxin Palace steward Linbiao happened to witness the whole exchange.
units.literal: At that moment an envoy from the office of Linbiao in the Changxin Palace happened to arrive and heard and saw it.

units.zh: 後上朝東宮，太后泣曰：「帝間顏色瘦黑，班侍中本大將軍所舉，宜寵異之，益求其比，以輔聖德。
units.en: Later, when the emperor came to court at the Eastern Palace, the Empress Dowager wept and said, "The emperor's complexion has lately grown thin and dark. Palace Attendant Ban was first recommended by the Grand General; he should receive exceptional favor. Seek out more men like him, so they may support your sagely virtue.
units.literal: Later, when the emperor attended court at the eastern palace, the Dowager wept and said, "The emperor's face lately looks thin and dark; Palace Attendant Ban was originally raised by the grand general—he should be favored above others; seek out more men like him to support sagely virtue.

units.zh: 宜遣富平侯且就國。」
units.en: She insisted that Marquis Zhang Fang of Fuping be ordered back to his estate for the time being."
units.literal: The Marquis of Fuping ought for the nonce to be sent to his fief."

units.zh: 上曰：「諾。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Yes."
units.literal: The emperor said, "Yes."

units.zh: 車騎將軍王音聞之，以風丞相御史奏富平侯罪過，上乃出放為邊都尉。
units.en: When General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Yin heard of this, he prompted the chancellor and the imperial counselor to memorialize the crimes of the Marquis of Fuping, Zhang Fang, and the emperor sent Fang out as a commandant on the frontier.
units.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Yin heard of it and prompted the chancellor and imperial clerk to memorialize Zhang Fang's crimes; the emperor thereupon sent Fang out as commandant of a border command.

units.zh: 後復徵入，太后與上書曰：「前所道尚未效，富平侯反復來，其能默虖？」
units.en: Later, when he was summoned back again, the Empress Dowager wrote to the emperor, saying, "What I spoke of before has still not taken effect, and now the Marquis of Fuping has come back again. How can I remain silent?"
units.literal: Later he was summoned back; the Dowager wrote to the emperor saying, "What I urged earlier has not yet taken effect, yet the Marquis of Fuping has returned—can I remain silent?"

units.zh: 上謝曰：「請今奉詔。」
units.en: The emperor apologized and said, "From now on I shall obey the edict."
units.literal: The emperor apologized and said, "From now on I shall obey the edict."

units.zh: 是時許商為少府，師丹為光祿勳，上於是引商、丹入為光祿大夫，伯遷水衡都尉，與兩師並侍中，皆秩中二千石。
units.en: At the time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants. The emperor brought Shang and Dan into court as grand counselors of the household, promoted Ban Bo to chief commandant of waters and parks, and had him serve as Palace Attendant together with his two teachers; all held the salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.
units.literal: At that time Xu Shang was Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Shi Dan was Chamberlain for Attendants; the emperor therefore brought Shang and Dan in as grand counselors of the household, Bo was promoted to chief commandant of waters and parks, and together with his two teachers he served as Palace Attendant, all at salary rank of fully two thousand piculs.

units.zh: 每朝東宮，常從；
units.en: Ban Bo routinely escorted the emperor to the Dowager's audiences;
units.literal: Whenever court was held at the eastern palace, he regularly accompanied the emperor;

units.zh: 及有大政，俱使諭指於公卿。
units.en: and whenever weighty policy arose, he and his colleagues carried the throne's instructions to the high ministers.
units.literal: when there were great policies, both were sent to convey the imperial intent to the dukes and ministers.

units.zh: 上亦稍厭游宴，復修經書之業，太后甚悅。
units.en: Cheng slowly lost his taste for pleasure trips and turned again to classical study, which delighted the Dowager.
units.literal: The emperor also gradually wearied of roaming feasts and returned to the work of the classics; the Dowager was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 丞相方進復奏，富平侯竟就國。
units.en: After another memorial from Chancellor Fangjin, Zhang Fang finally went to his estate for good.
units.literal: Chancellor Fangjin again memorialized, and the Marquis of Fuping was at last sent to his fief.

units.zh: 會伯病卒，年三十八，朝廷愍惜焉。
units.en: Ban Bo soon died of illness at thirty-eight, and the court mourned the loss.
units.literal: It chanced that Bo died of illness at age thirty-eight, and the court pitied him.

units.zh: 斿博學有俊材，左將軍師丹舉賢良方正，以對策為議郎，遷諫大夫、右曹中郎將，與劉向校祕書。
units.en: Ban You had a capacious mind; Shi Dan nominated him worthy and upright, his policy essay won him a consultant post, and he rose to remonstrant grandee and right colonel of the gentlemen while collating palace archives beside Liu Xiang.
units.literal: You was broadly learned and possessed outstanding talent; General of the Left Shi Dan recommended him as worthy and upright; by his examination answers he became a gentleman consultant, was promoted to grandee remonstrant and colonel of the gentlemen on the right staff, and collated the secretariat books with Liu Xiang.

units.zh: 每奏事，斿以選受詔進讀群書。
units.en: Whenever memorials reached the throne, Ban You was the reader the emperor picked to intone the palace collection.
units.literal: Whenever documents were presented, You was selected to receive edicts and read aloud the collected books.

units.zh: 上器其能，賜以祕書之副。
units.en: Cheng prized his skill enough to gift him facsimile sets of the rare books.
units.literal: The sovereign valued his ability and granted him duplicate copies of the secretariat texts.

units.zh: 時書不布，自東平思王以叔父求太史公、諸子書，大將軍白不許。
units.en: Because palace books were still withheld from the public, the Prince of Dongping's request, as imperial uncle, for Sima Qian's histories and the masters' treatises was refused when the Grand General reported against it.
units.literal: At that time books were not circulated abroad; when the Prince of Dongping, as paternal uncle, asked for the Grand Scribe's records and the masters' writings, the grand general reported that it should not be allowed.

units.zh: 語在東平王傳。
units.en: The full story appears in the prince's biography.
units.literal: The account is given in the biography of the Prince of Dongping.

units.zh: 斿亦早卒，有子曰嗣，顯名當世。
units.en: Ban You died young as well, leaving a son Si who won renown in that generation.
units.literal: You also died young; he had a son named Si, who became famous in his own day.

units.zh: 穉少為黃門郎中常侍，方直自守。
units.en: In his youth Ban Zhi served as a Yellow Gate Gentleman and Palace Attendant and maintained strict integrity.
units.literal: In his youth Ban Zhi served as a Yellow Gate Gentleman and Palace Attendant and maintained strict integrity.

units.zh: 成帝季年，立定陶王為太子，數遣中盾請問近臣，穉獨不敢答。
units.en: Late in Cheng's reign, when the Prince of Dingtao was named heir, the heir's agents quizzed every intimate attendant, but Ban Zhi alone refused to reply.
units.literal: In the last years of Emperor Cheng, when the Prince of Dingtao was established as heir apparent, the heir repeatedly sent the palace shield to inquire of the attendants at his side, and Zhi alone dared not answer.

units.zh: 哀帝即位，出穉為西河屬國都尉，遷廣平相。
units.en: Emperor Ai posted him chief commandant over the Xihe dependent state, then promoted him to chancellor of Guangping.
units.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended the throne, Zhi was sent out as chief commandant of dependent states for Xihe and was promoted to chancellor of Guangping.

units.zh: 王莽少與穉兄弟同列友善，兄事斿而弟畜穉。
units.en: While young, Wang Mang was friendly with Ban Zhi and his brothers, who served alongside him. He treated Ban You as an elder brother and Ban Zhi as a younger one.
units.literal: When young, Wang Mang sat in the same rank as the brothers Zhi, friendly with them; he treated You as an elder brother and kept Zhi as a younger brother.

units.zh: 斿之卒也，修緦麻，賻賵甚厚。
units.en: When Ban You died, Wang Mang donned mourning hemp and gave lavish funeral gifts.
units.literal: When You died, he wore the hemp of mourning and gave funeral gifts very generously.

units.zh: 平帝即位，太后臨朝，莽秉政，方欲文致太平，使使者分行風俗，采頌聲，而穉無所上。
units.en: After Emperor Ping took the throne, the Dowager regent and Wang Mang in power sought to polish the age into Great Peace, dispatching envoys to survey local customs and collect praise songs, but Ban Zhi sent nothing up.
units.literal: When Emperor Ping ascended the throne, the Dowager held court and Mang held power; just then wishing to adorn and bring about Great Peace, he sent envoys to travel the customs in separate routes and gather songs of praise, yet Zhi submitted nothing.

units.zh: 琅邪太守公孫閎言災害於公府，大司空甄豐遣屬馳至兩郡諷吏民，而劾閎空造不祥，穉絕嘉應，嫉害聖政，皆不道。
units.en: Langye administrator Gongsun Hong reported disasters to the capital; Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent aides racing to both commanderies to warn officials and people, then impeached Hong for inventing ill omens and Zhi for withholding auspicious responses and obstructing the sage government—both accused of capital crimes.
units.literal: The Administrator of Langye, Gongsun Hong, reported disasters to the public offices. Grand Minister of Works Zhen Feng sent subordinates post-haste to both commanderies to admonish officials and commoners, then impeached Hong for fabricating ill omens and Zhi for suppressing auspicious responses and obstructing sagely government; both were accused of capital crimes.

units.zh: 太后曰：「不宣德美，宜與言災害者異罰。
units.en: The Dowager said, "Failing to proclaim virtue deserves a different penalty from reporting disasters.
units.literal: The Dowager said, "One who does not spread virtue and beauty ought to receive a different punishment from one who speaks of disasters.

units.zh: 且後宮賢家，我所哀也。」
units.en: And this is a worthy family of the rear palace, whom I pity."
units.literal: Moreover, this is a worthy house of the rear palace—I pity them."

units.zh: 閎獨下獄誅。
units.en: Gongsun Hong alone was imprisoned and executed.
units.literal: Hong alone was sent down to prison and executed.

units.zh: 穉懼，上書陳恩謝罪，願歸相印，入補延陵園郎，太后許焉。
units.en: Ban Zhi, afraid, memorialized his gratitude and apology, asked to surrender the chancellor seal, and sought appointment as a gentleman of Yanling Park; the Dowager agreed.
units.literal: Zhi was afraid; he submitted a memorial stating his grace and apologizing for guilt, wishing to return the chancellor seal and enter service as a gentleman of Yanling Park; the Dowager granted it.

units.zh: 食故祿終身。
units.en: He drew his former stipend for the rest of his life.
units.literal: He received his former salary for life.

units.zh: 由是班氏不顯莽朝，亦不罹咎。
units.en: Thereafter the Ban house kept out of Wang Mang's limelight and escaped punishment as well.
units.literal: From this the Ban clan did not stand out in Mang's court, yet also did not suffer blame.

units.zh: 初，成帝性寬，進入直言，是以王音、翟方進等繩法舉過，而劉向、杜鄴、王章、朱雲之徒肆意犯上，故自帝師安昌侯，諸舅大將軍兄弟及公卿大夫、後宮外屬史許之家有貴寵者，莫不被文傷詆。
units.en: Cheng's easy temper invited blunt speech, so ministers such as Wang Yin and Zhai Fangjin policed the law while scholars like Liu Xiang, Du Ye, Wang Zhang, and Zhu Yun flayed the throne; from the imperial tutor the marquis of Anchang through the Wang uncles and every powerful consort kin of the Shi and Xu lines, no favorite escaped their written attacks.
units.literal: In the beginning, Emperor Cheng's nature was lenient, and those who entered remonstrated bluntly; therefore Wang Yin, Zhai Fangjin, and others applied the law and reported faults, while Liu Xiang, Du Ye, Wang Zhang, Zhu Yun, and their sort wantonly offended the throne; thus from the emperor's teacher the Marquis of Anchang down to the great uncles the grand general and his brothers, dukes, ministers, grandees, and the households of the rear-palace affines surnamed Shi and Xu who enjoyed favor and power, there was none who was not wounded by their writings and slandered.

units.zh: 唯谷永嘗言「建始、河平之際，許、班之貴，傾動前朝，熏灼四方，賞賜無量，空虛內臧，女寵至極，不可尚矣；
units.en: Only Gu Yong once said, "During the Jianshi and Heping eras, the eminence of the Xu and Ban houses shook the former court and blazed across the four quarters. Rewards and gifts were beyond measure; they emptied the inner treasury, and favor shown to women reached an unsurpassable extreme;
units.literal: Only Gu Yong once said, "In the Jianshi and Heping era the eminence of the Xu and Ban houses shook the previous court, scorched the four quarters, and their gifts had no measure; they emptied the inner treasury; favor to women reached an extreme that could not be surpassed;

units.zh: 今之後起，天所不饗，什倍於前。」
units.en: while the new crop of favorites, heaven-rejected, would outdo them tenfold."
units.literal: those who rise afterward, whom Heaven will not bless, are ten times what went before."

units.zh: 永指以駮譏趙、李，亦無間云。
units.en: He aimed the rebuke at Zhao Feiyan and Li Ping, yet commentators say no one could gainsay his point.
units.literal: Yong pointed with this to refute and ridicule Zhao and Li, yet none could find fault with it, it is said.

units.zh: 穉生彪。
units.en: Ban Zhi was the father of Ban Biao.
units.literal: Zhi begat Biao.

units.zh: 彪字叔皮，幼與從兄嗣共遊學，家有賜書，內足於財，好古之士自遠方至，父黨揚子雲以下莫不造門。
units.en: Ban Biao, styled Shuipi, studied abroad with his cousin Ban Si while the household enjoyed imperial book grants and deep coffers, drawing classicists from afar so that even Yang Xiong and his father's circle beat a path to their door.
units.literal: Biao, courtesy name Shuipi, in youth roamed in study with his elder cousin Si; the family possessed books granted by the throne and was ample in wealth, so lovers of antiquity came from distant regions, and from Yang Xiong downward none of his father's associates failed to visit the gate.

units.zh: 嗣雖修儒學，然貴老嚴之術。
units.en: Ban Si pursued Confucian texts yet revered the Daoist teachings of Laozi and Yan Junping.
units.literal: Although Si cultivated Confucian learning, he honored the arts of Laozi and Yan Junping.

units.zh: 桓生欲借其書，嗣報曰：「若夫嚴子者，絕聖棄智，修生保真，清虛澹泊，歸之自然，獨師友造化，而不為世俗所役者也。
units.en: When Huan Sheng wished to borrow his books, Ban Si replied, "As for Master Yan, he cut off sagehood and discarded cleverness, cultivated life and guarded the genuine, was clear, empty, and still, and returned to the natural; he took only creation as teacher and friend and was not enslaved by the vulgar world.
units.literal: When Huan Sheng wished to borrow his books, Si replied, "As for Master Yan, he cut off sagehood and discarded cleverness, cultivated life and guarded the genuine, was clear, empty, and still, and returned to the natural; he took only creation as teacher and friend and was not enslaved by the vulgar world.

units.zh: 漁釣於一壑，則萬物不奸其志；
units.en: If he angled in one gully, then the myriad things could not corrupt his purpose;
units.literal: If he angled in one gully, then the myriad things could not corrupt his purpose;

units.zh: 栖遲於一丘，則天下不易其樂。
units.en: if he rested on one hill, then all under Heaven could not alter his joy.
units.literal: if he rested on one hill, then all under Heaven could not alter his joy.

units.zh: 不絓聖人之罔，不齅驕君之餌，蕩然肆志，談者不得而名焉，故可貴也。
units.en: Such a man never walked into the sages' snares or nibbled a proud king's hook; he wandered beyond labels, which is why he is worth imitating.
units.literal: He was not caught in the nets of the sages, did not sniff at the bait of arrogant lords, roamed at will where talkers could not pin a name on him—therefore he was admirable.

units.zh: 今吾子已貫仁誼之羈絆，繫名聲之韁鎖，伏周、孔之軌躅，馳顏、閔之極摯，既繫攣於世教矣，何用大道為自眩曜？
units.en: Now you, sir, have already put on the fetters of benevolence and duty and tied yourself to the reins and locks of reputation. You crouch in the tracks of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius and race toward the utmost earnestness of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian; since you are already bound fast by worldly teaching, why use the great Way merely to dazzle yourself?
units.literal: Now you, sir, have already passed through the hobbles of benevolence and duty, are tethered by the bridle of reputation, tread in the tracks of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, and gallop to the utmost earnestness of Yan and Min; you are already bound by worldly instruction—why use the great Way to dazzle yourself?

units.zh: 昔有學步於邯鄲者。
units.en: There was once a man who went to Handan to learn a new way of walking.
units.literal: Formerly there was one who learned to walk in Handan.

units.zh: 曾未得其髣彿，又復失其故步，遂匍匐而歸耳！
units.en: Before mastering the strut he forgot his own walk and had to crawl home in shame.
units.literal: Before he had grasped even a semblance of it, he again lost his native step, so he crawled home!

units.zh: 恐似此類，故不進。」
units.en: Lest your borrowing end the same way, I decline to lend the books."
units.literal: I fear it would be like this sort of thing; therefore I do not advance them."

units.zh: 嗣之行己持論如此。
units.en: Such was Ban Si's conduct and the tone of his debate.
units.literal: Thus Si conducted himself and framed his arguments.

units.zh: 叔皮唯聖人之道然後盡心焉。
units.en: Ban Biao reserved his full devotion for the path of the sages alone.
units.literal: Shuipi devoted his whole heart only to the Way of the sages.

units.zh: 年二十，遭王莽敗，世祖即位於冀州。
units.en: At twenty he lived through Wang Mang's fall and watched Liu Xiu raise the Han banner in Ji.
units.literal: At twenty he encountered Wang Mang's collapse, and the Founding Ancestor took the throne in Ji Province.

units.zh: 時隗囂據壟擁眾，招輯英俊，而公孫述稱帝於蜀漢，天下雲擾，大者連州郡，小者據縣邑。
units.en: Wei Xiao then blocked the Long road and recruited talent while Gongsun Shu styled himself emperor in Shu; the realm splintered into rival zones large and small.
units.literal: At that time Wei Xiao held Long and gathered heroes, while Gongsun Shu declared himself emperor in Shu-Han; all under Heaven boiled like a cloud; the great linked commanderies and the small seized counties.

units.zh: 囂問彪曰：「往者周亡，戰國並爭，天下分裂，數世然後乃定，其抑者從橫之事復起於今乎？
units.en: Wei Xiao asked Ban Biao, "In former times when Zhou fell, the Warring States strove together and the realm split apart, and only after several generations was it settled—will the affairs of vertical and horizontal alliances rise again now,
units.literal: Xiao asked Biao, "In former times when Zhou fell, the Warring States strove together, the realm split apart, and only after several generations was it settled—will the affairs of vertical and horizontal alliances rise again now?

units.zh: 將承運迭興在於一人也？
units.en: or will the received mandate pass in turn and concentrate in a single man?
units.literal: Or will the received mandate pass in turn and concentrate in a single man?

units.zh: 願先生論之。」
units.en: He begged Ban Biao to give his reading."
units.literal: I beg the master to discuss it."

units.zh: 對曰：「周之廢興與漢異。
units.en: He replied, "The decline and rise of Zhou differ from those of Han.
units.literal: He replied, "The decline and rise of Zhou differ from those of Han.

units.zh: 昔周立爵五等，諸侯從政，本根既微，枝葉強大，故其末流有從橫之事，其勢然也。
units.en: Zhou had enfeoffed powerful barons whose branches overshadowed the crown, which is why the age of alliances followed inevitably.
units.literal: In olden times Zhou established five ranks of nobles; the feudal lords administered government; the root was already weak while the branches grew mighty; therefore in its last currents there were vertical-and-horizontal intrigues—the tendency made it so.

units.zh: 漢家承秦之制，並立郡縣，主有專己之威，臣無百年之柄，至於成帝，假借外家，哀、平短祚，國嗣三絕，危自上起，傷不及下。
units.en: Han copied Qin's commandery system so the emperor kept iron control while ministers lacked hereditary leverage; down to Cheng the consort clans borrowed authority, Ai and Ping died young, the succession failed thrice, yet the rot started in the palace, not among the people.
units.literal: The house of Han inherited Qin's system and set up commanderies and counties together; the ruler holds unchecked personal authority and ministers lack handles that last a century; down to Emperor Cheng the outer families were lent power, Ai and Ping enjoyed short reigns, the imperial succession failed three times, the danger began at the top, and harm did not reach below.

units.zh: 故王氏之貴，傾擅朝廷，能竊號位，而不根於民。
units.en: Thus the Wangs could bully the court and seize the throne in name, but they never sank roots in the common folk.
units.literal: Therefore the eminence of the Wang house dominated the court and could usurp titles and the mandate, yet it struck no root among the people.

units.zh: 是以即真之後，天下莫不引領而歎，十餘年間，外內騷擾，遠近俱發，假號雲合，咸稱劉氏，不謀而同辭。
units.en: Once Wang Mang mounted the throne as emperor, the realm looked on with clenched throats; within a decade rebellion boiled inside the borders and out, every quarter flew false Liu banners, and men who had never conspired used the same slogan.
units.literal: Therefore after he took the true throne, none under Heaven failed to crane their necks and sigh; within a dozen years disturbance raged within and without, near and far rose together, false titles swarmed like clouds, all called themselves Liu, and without planning they spoke with one voice.

units.zh: 方今雄桀帶州城者，皆無七國世業之資。
units.en: Today's strongmen who sit on walled prefectures command none of the old Warring States' hereditary depth.
units.literal: Now those heroic men who hold commanderies and cities all lack the inherited capital of the Seven States.

units.zh: 詩云：『皇矣上帝，臨下有赫，鑒觀四方，求民之莫。』
units.en: As the Greater Odes put it: 'Sublime is God on high, terrible in His gaze across the realm, searching out where the people may find peace.'
units.literal: The Odes say: 'August indeed is God on high, awesome as He looks down; He surveys the four quarters and seeks the people's rest.'

units.zh: 今民皆謳吟思漢，鄉仰劉氏，已可知矣。」
units.en: The folk already sing of their longing for Han and lift their eyes to the Liu name, which tells you all you need to know."
units.literal: Now the people all chant and sigh, thinking of Han and yearning for the Liu house—this can already be known."

units.zh: 囂曰：「先生言周、漢之勢，可也，至於但見愚民習識劉氏姓號之故，而謂漢家復興，疏矣！
units.en: Wei Xiao said, "What you say, sir, about the tendencies of Zhou and Han is acceptable, but to infer from the mere fact that foolish commoners are habituated to the Liu surname that the house of Han will rise again is far too loose!
units.literal: Xiao said, "What you say, sir, about the tendencies of Zhou and Han is acceptable, but to infer from the mere fact that foolish commoners are habituated to the Liu surname that the house of Han will rise again is far too loose!

units.zh: 昔秦失其鹿，劉季逐而掎之，時民復知漢虖！」
units.en: In olden times Qin lost the deer, and Liu Ji chased and seized it—did the people then even know there would be a Han?"
units.literal: In olden times Qin lost the deer, and Liu Ji chased and seized it—did the people then even know there would be a Han?"

units.zh: 既感囂言，又愍狂狡之不息，乃著王命論以救時難。
units.en: Half persuaded by Wei Xiao yet sick of endless adventurism, Ban Biao drafted the Discourse on the King's Mandate to steady a chaotic age.
units.literal: Having been moved by Xiao's words and also pitying that wild cunning would not cease, he thereupon composed the Discourse on the King's Mandate to rescue the troubles of the age.

units.zh: 其辭曰：
units.en: The text runs as follows:
units.literal: Its words say:

units.zh: 昔在帝堯之禪曰：「咨爾舜，天之曆數在爾躬。」
units.en: When Emperor Yao yielded the throne he said, "Shun, the numbered seasons of Heaven now sit on you."
units.literal: In olden times, at Yao's abdication it was said, "Ah, you Shun, Heaven's reckoned succession rests in your person."

units.zh: 舜亦以命禹。
units.en: Shun passed the same charge to Yu.
units.literal: Shun also used these words to command Yu.

units.zh: 臮于稷𢍆，咸佐唐虞，光濟四海，奕世載德，至于湯武，而有天下。
units.en: Through ministers such as Hou Ji and Xie the virtue of Yao and Shun spread across the seas, generation on generation, until Tang of Shang and Wu of Zhou inherited the whole realm.
units.literal: Down to Ji and Xie, all assisted Tang and Yu, their brilliance aiding the four seas; age after age they bore accumulated virtue, down to Tang and Wu, and thus possessed all under Heaven.

units.zh: 雖其遭遇異時，禪代不同，至于應天順民，其揆一也。
units.en: Their circumstances and transfers of power varied, yet each case matched Heaven's will and the people's heart in the same way.
units.literal: Although their encounters differed in time and abdication differed in form, as for responding to Heaven and following the people, the measure was one.

units.zh: 是故劉氏承堯之祚，氏族之世，著乎春秋。
units.en: The Liu lineage thus continued Yao's mandate, a pedigree the Spring and Autumn Annals already recorded.
units.literal: Therefore the Liu house received Yao's blessing, and the generations of the clan are set down in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

units.zh: 唐據火德，而漢紹之，始起沛澤，則神母夜號，以章赤帝之符。
units.en: Emperor Yao held the virtue of Fire, and Han succeeded it; when it first arose in the Pei marshes, the divine mother cried out in the night to manifest the token of the Red Emperor.
units.literal: Tang held the virtue of Fire, and Han succeeded it; when it first arose in Pei marsh, the divine mother cried out in the night to manifest the token of the Red Emperor.

units.zh: 由是言之，帝王之祚，必有明聖顯懿之德，豐功厚利積絫之業，然後精誠通於神明，流澤加於生民，故能為鬼神所福饗，天下所歸往，未見運世無本，功德不紀，而得屈起在此位者也。
units.en: Imperial fortune, in short, demands luminous virtue and piled-up achievements before the spirits answer and the people rally; no one seizes the dragon throne from thin air with neither merit nor mandate.
units.literal: From this it may be said that the blessing of emperors and kings must rest on manifest sagely and brilliant virtue, on enterprises of abundant merit and thick benefit piled up layer upon layer; only then does essential sincerity penetrate the spirits, flowing favor reaches the living people, and therefore they can be blessed and feasted by ghosts and gods and be the object to which all under Heaven turns; one has never seen a ruler without root in the age's fortune, without recorded merit and virtue, who could yet vault up and occupy this position.

units.zh: 世俗見高祖興於布衣，不達其故，以為適遭暴亂，得奮其劍，游說之士至比天下於逐鹿，幸捷而得之，不知神器有命，不可以智力求也。
units.en: Common opinion mistakes Gaozu for a lucky swordsman who grabbed power in chaos, the "deer hunt" cliché of rhetoricians; they miss that the sacred vessel answers only to fate, not to cunning or muscle.
units.literal: The vulgar world, seeing the Founding Ancestor rise from common cloth and not penetrating the reason, thinks he simply met violent disorder, was able to brandish his sword, and that wandering persuaders liken all under Heaven to chasing a deer, getting it by a lucky grab; they do not know that the divine regalia have a destined possessor and cannot be sought by wit or force.

units.zh: 悲夫！
units.en: A bitter pity.
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 此世所以多亂臣賊子者也。
units.en: That blindness is why treason and usurpation multiply.
units.literal: This is why the age has so many traitorous ministers and rebellious sons.

units.zh: 若然者，豈徒闇於天道哉？
units.en: If that were the whole story, would the fault lie only in misunderstanding Heaven?
units.literal: If it is so, is it only darkness about the Way of Heaven?

units.zh: 又不睹之於人事矣！
units.en: They have not even looked at the evidence of human affairs.
units.literal: They have also failed to observe it in human affairs!

units.zh: 夫餓饉流隸，飢寒道路，思有裋褐之褻，儋石之畜，所願不過一金，然終於轉死溝壑。
units.en: Starving drifters on the highway dream only of a patched coat or a sack of grain, a few coins of wealth, and still rot in the ditch.
units.literal: As for the starving vagrants, the famished on the roads who long for the mean comfort of a short coat and the store of a peck or two of grain, whose desires reach no further than a single piece of gold, yet in the end they die turned over in ditches and gullies.

units.zh: 何則？
units.en: Why should that be?
units.literal: Why is it so?

units.zh: 貧窮亦有命也。
units.en: Even poverty and plenty ride an appointed lot.
units.literal: Want and wealth also have their allotted fate.

units.zh: 況虖天子之貴，四海之富，神明之祚，可得而妄處哉？
units.en: How then could anyone lightly seize the Son of Heaven's rank, the wealth of the realm, and the spirits' favor?
units.literal: How much more the honor of the Son of Heaven, the riches of the four seas, the blessing of the spirits—can these be seized recklessly?

units.zh: 故雖遭罹阨會，竊其權柄，勇如信、布，彊如梁、籍，成如王莽，然卒潤鑊伏質，亨醢分裂，又況幺{麻骨}，尚不及數子，而欲闇奸天位者虖！
units.en: Though men may seize power in a moment of crisis, even those as brave as Han Xin and Ying Bu, as strong as Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu, or as successful as Wang Mang ended boiled in cauldrons, laid on the block, pickled, or torn apart. How much less should petty men beneath them covertly covet the throne?
units.literal: Therefore although they encountered hard straits and usurped the handles of power—brave as Xin and Bu, strong as Liang and Ji, accomplished as Wang Mang—still in the end they were boiled in the cauldron, exposed on the chopping block, diced in pickle and torn apart; how much more trifling mites who do not match those men yet would darkly encroach on Heaven's seat!

units.zh: 是故駑蹇之乘不騁千里之塗，燕雀之疇不奮六翮之用，楶梲之材不荷棟梁之任，斗筲之子不秉帝王之重。
units.en: A cripple nag cannot run the thousand-mile road, sparrows cannot soar like great birds, splinter wood will not roof a hall, and a small-minded man cannot wear the crown.
units.literal: Therefore a lame gelding does not gallop a thousand-li course; a flock of swallows and sparrows does not spread six-pinioned flight; rafter-end wood cannot bear the load of beams and pillars; a peck-and dipper fellow cannot sustain the weight of emperors and kings.

units.zh: 易曰「鼎折足，覆公餗」，不勝其任也。
units.en: The Changes say, "The tripod breaks its legs and spills the duke's gruel," meaning it could not bear the burden.
units.literal: The Changes say, "The tripod breaks its legs and spills the duke's gruel," meaning it could not bear the burden.

units.zh: 當秦之末，豪桀共推陳嬰而王之，嬰母止之曰：「自吾為子家婦，而世貧賤，卒富貴不祥，不如以兵屬人，事成少受其利，不成禍有所歸。」
units.en: At the end of Qin, local strongmen together urged Chen Ying to accept the title of king. His mother stopped him, saying, "Ever since I became a daughter-in-law in your family, we have been poor and lowly for generations. Sudden wealth and honor would be inauspicious. Better to place the troops under someone else: if the undertaking succeeds, you will receive a small share of the benefit; if it fails, the disaster will fall elsewhere."
units.literal: At the end of Qin, the bold men together urged Chen Ying to take the kingly title; Ying's mother stopped him, saying, "Ever since I became your family's daughter-in-law, generation after generation we have been poor and base; to end in wealth and honor is inauspicious; better to hand the troops to another—if the affair succeeds you will receive a little benefit; if it fails disaster will have somewhere to go."

units.zh: 嬰從其言，而陳氏以寧。
units.en: Chen Ying obeyed, and his house survived the wars unscathed.
units.literal: Ying followed her words, and the Chen clan thereby enjoyed peace.

units.zh: 王陵之母亦見項氏之必亡，而劉氏之將興也。
units.en: Wang Ling's mother likewise saw that the Xiang clan would fall and the Liu house would rise.
units.literal: The mother of Wang Ling also saw that the Xiang clan was sure to perish and the Liu house was about to rise.

units.zh: 是時陵為漢將，而母獲於楚，有漢使來，陵母見之，謂曰：「願告吾子，漢王長者，必得天下，子謹事之，無有二心。」
units.en: While Wang Ling served Han, his mother was held by Chu; meeting a Han envoy, she said to him, "I beg you tell my son: the King of Han is a man of generous nature and is sure to gain all under Heaven; let him serve him carefully and harbor no second heart."
units.literal: At that time Ling was a Han general, but his mother had been taken by Chu; when a Han envoy arrived, Ling's mother saw him and said to him, "I beg you tell my son: the King of Han is a man of generous nature and is sure to gain all under Heaven; let him serve him carefully and harbor no second heart.

units.zh: 遂對漢使伏劍而死，以固勉陵。
units.en: She then drew a blade before the envoy and fell dead to steel her son's resolve.
units.literal: She thereupon fell on a sword before the Han envoy and died, thereby to firm Ling's resolve.

units.zh: 其後果定於漢，陵為宰相封侯。
units.en: Han triumphed, Wang Ling rose to chancellor, and ennoblement followed.
units.literal: Afterward it was indeed settled with Han, and Ling became chancellor and was enfeoffed as marquis.

units.zh: 夫以匹婦之明，猶能推事理之致，探禍福之機，而全宗祀於無窮，垂策書於春秋，而況大丈夫之事虖！
units.en: If a woman's wit could read fate, save her lineage, and earn a line in the annals, how much more should a grown man grasp the mandate!
units.literal: If by the insight of a mere woman one can still push principle to its limit, probe the pivot of fortune and disaster, and preserve the ancestral sacrifices without end, leaving one's plan in the Spring and Autumn Annals, how much more the affairs of a great husband!

units.zh: 是故窮達有命，吉凶由人，嬰母知廢，陵母知興，審此四者，帝王之分決矣。
units.en: Fortune governs rise and fall, yet human choice steers blessing or curse; Chen's mother knew whom to quit, Wang's mother knew whom to back, and those four judgments settle who may be king.
units.literal: Therefore failure and success have their allotted fate, good and ill come from men; Ying's mother knew what to abolish, Ling's mother knew what would rise; when these four points are examined, the portion of emperors and kings is decided.

units.zh: 蓋在高祖，其興也有五：一曰帝堯之苗裔，二曰體貌多奇異，三曰神武有徵應，四曰寬明而仁恕，五曰知人善任使。
units.en: Gaozu's ascent rested on five signs: Yao's bloodline, a singular physique, omens that blessed his arms, a generous humane temper, and a gift for placing the right men.
units.literal: As for the Founding Ancestor, there were five reasons for his rise: first, he was a descendant of Emperor Yao; second, his body and appearance held many marvels; third, his divine martial prowess had confirming omens; fourth, he was lenient, enlightened, humane, and forgiving; fifth, he knew men and employed them well.

units.zh: 加之以信誠好謀，達於聽受，見善如不及，用人如由己，從諫如順流，趣時如嚮赴；
units.en: He was candid, loved strategy, listened well, chased every good counsel, handed offices as freely as if they were his own limbs, took advice like running water, and seized each moment as though answering a call;
units.literal: Add to this that he was trustworthy, sincere, fond of planning, open in hearing and accepting counsel; he saw good as if he could not catch up, employed men as if using himself, followed remonstrance like going with the current, and hastened to the timely moment as if answering a summons;

units.zh: 當食吐哺，納子房之策；
units.en: he spat out a mouthful mid-meal to enact Zhang Liang's scheme;
units.literal: when it was time to eat he spat out the food in his mouth, adopting Zifang's plan;

units.zh: 拔足揮洗，揖酈生之說；
units.en: he broke off his bath to salute Li Yiji's plea;
units.literal: he stopped washing his feet and received Lisheng's proposal with a bow;

units.zh: 寤戍卒之言，斷懷土之情；
units.en: he heeded a guardsman's plea and checked his homesick march;
units.literal: he awoke to the words of garrison soldiers and cut short his longing for native soil;

units.zh: 高四皓之名，割肌膚之愛；
units.en: he courted the Four Elders though it cost him a father's love;
units.literal: he prized the fame of the Four Hoary Ones and sliced flesh-close affection;

units.zh: 舉韓信於行陳，收陳平於亡命，英雄陳力，群策畢舉：此高祖之大略，所以成帝業也。
units.en: He pulled Han Xin from the ranks, rescued Chen Ping from flight, and let every able man lend strength until the imperial work was done.
units.literal: he raised Han Xin from the ranks of battle and gathered Chen Ping from life as a fugitive; heroes deployed their strength, every stratagem was offered: this was the Founding Ancestor's grand design whereby he completed the imperial enterprise.

units.zh: 若乃靈瑞符應，又可略聞矣。
units.en: The portents that marked him deserve a word as well.
units.literal: As for numinous omens and confirming tokens, one may also hear them in outline.

units.zh: 初劉媼任高祖而夢與神遇，震電晦冥，有龍蛇之怪。
units.en: Lady Liu dreamed of a spirit when she conceived him; thunder rolled in black sky and dragon shapes writhed.
units.literal: At first, when the elder Liu was pregnant with the Founding Ancestor, she dreamed of meeting a spirit; lightning flashed and the darkness was murky, with prodigies of dragons and serpents.

units.zh: 及其長而多靈，有異於眾，是以王、武感物而折券，呂公睹形而進女；
units.en: As he matured, uncanny signs set him apart, so Wang and Wu tore up old debts at a glance and Lü Gong married him a daughter for his bearing;
units.literal: When he grew and showed many spiritual signs, different from the multitude, therefore Wang and Wu were moved by things and tore their bonds, and Duke Lü, seeing his form, advanced his daughter;

units.zh: 秦皇東游以厭其氣，呂后望雲而知所處；
units.en: the Qin First Emperor toured east to smother his qi, while Empress Lü read clouds to find him;
units.literal: the First Emperor of Qin toured east to suppress his aura, and Empress Lü watched clouds to know where he dwelt;

units.zh: 始受命則白蛇分，西入關則五星聚。
units.en: His first mandate split the white serpent, and the five planets clustered when he entered the passes.
units.literal: when he first received the mandate the white serpent was cleft; when he entered Guan in the west the five planets gathered.

units.zh: 故淮陰、留侯謂之天授，非人力也。
units.en: Han Xin and Zhang Liang called such things Heaven's investiture, not mortal striving.
units.literal: Therefore the Marquis of Huaiyin and the Marquis of Liu called it Heaven's gift, not human power.

units.zh: 歷古今之得失，驗行事之成敗，稽帝王之世運，考五者之所謂，取舍不厭斯位，符瑞不同斯度，而苟昧於權利，越次妄據，外不量力，內不知命，則必喪保家之主，失天年之壽，遇折足之凶，伏鈇鉞之誅。
units.en: Review the gains and losses of past and present, test the success and failure of deeds, examine the age's fortunes of emperors and kings, and consider what is meant by the five signs. If one's choices do not fit that position and one's auspicious signs do not match that measure, yet one is blinded by power and profit, oversteps the order, and occupies it recklessly, without measuring one's strength outwardly or knowing the mandate inwardly, then one will surely lose the lord who preserves the house, forfeit the full span of life, meet the ill omen of the broken leg, and submit to execution by axe and halberd.
units.literal: Reviewing the gains and losses of ancient and modern times, testing the success and failure of deeds done, examining the age's fortune of emperors and kings, investigating what these five mean, if in choosing and rejecting one does not shrink from this position, if auspicious tokens do not match this measure, yet one blindly covets power and profit, leaps out of order and occupies it rashly, outwardly not measuring strength, inwardly not knowing fate, then one is sure to lose the lord who could preserve the family, forfeit the years Heaven grants, meet the misfortune of broken legs, and lie under the executioner's axe and halberd.

units.zh: 英雄誠知覺寤，畏若禍戒，超然遠覽，淵然深識，收陵、嬰之明分，絕信、布之覬覦，距逐鹿之瞽說，審神器之有授，毋貪不可幾，為二母之所咲，則福祚流于子孫，天祿其永終矣。
units.en: Had men of ambition truly awakened to these warnings, looked far, and understood deeply; had they heeded the clear judgment shown in the stories of Wang Ling and Chen Ying, abandoned Han Xin and Ying Bu's ambitions, rejected blind talk of chasing the deer, and recognized that the imperial regalia have a destined recipient; had they not grasped at the unattainable and made themselves a laughingstock to those two mothers, then blessings would have flowed to their descendants and Heaven's bounty endured.
units.literal: If heroes truly awaken in fear as if to omens of disaster, stand aloof with far-ranging sight, plumb the depths with silent understanding, take to heart the clear portions shown by Ling and Ying, cut off the covetous glances of Xin and Bu, reject the blind talk of deer-chasing, examine that the divine regalia have a recipient, do not greedily grasp what cannot be approached, and avoid being laughed at by the two mothers, then blessing and rank will flow to their sons and grandsons and Heaven's stipend will end only with time.

units.zh: 知隗囂終不寤，乃避墬於河西。
units.en: Seeing that Wei Xiao would never see reason, Ban Biao crossed to the Hexi corridor beyond the Yellow River.
units.literal: Knowing that Wei Xiao would never awaken, he therefore fled turmoil to the west of the River.

units.zh: 河西大將軍竇融嘉其美德，訪問焉。
units.en: Dou Rong, general of the west, admired his character and sought him out.
units.literal: The great general of Hexi, Dou Rong, admired his fine virtue and paid him visits.

units.zh: 舉茂材，為徐令，以病去官。
units.en: Nominated for outstanding talent, he served as magistrate of Xu until illness drove him home.
units.literal: He was nominated as an outstanding talent, became magistrate of Xu, and resigned office on account of illness.

units.zh: 後數應三公之召。
units.en: Later the three highest ministers repeatedly called him to office.
units.literal: Later he several times answered summons from the three dukes.

units.zh: 仕不為祿，所如不合；
units.en: He never took a post for the stipend, and each appointment chafed;
units.literal: In serving he did not seek salary; wherever he went it did not suit him;

units.zh: 學不為人，博而不俗；
units.en: He studied for truth, not for show, wide-ranging yet never coarse;
units.literal: in learning he did not study for others; he was broad yet not vulgar;

units.zh: 言不為華，述而不作。
units.en: His words stayed plain: he expounded the classics rather than inventing flashy prose.
units.literal: in speech he did not seek flowers; he transmitted and did not compose.

units.zh: 有子曰固，弱冠而孤，作幽通之賦，以致命遂志。
units.en: His son Ban Gu, orphaned at twenty, wrote the Rhapsody on Communicating with the Hidden to set his life on record.
units.literal: He had a son named Gu; at the capping age he was orphaned, and he composed the Rhapsody on Communicating with the Hidden to commit his mind to his chosen course.

units.zh: 其辭曰：
units.en: The piece begins:
units.literal: Its words say:

units.zh: 系高頊之玄冑兮，氏中葉之炳靈，繇凱風而蟬蛻兮，雄朔野以颺聲。
units.en: I am sprung from Zhuanxu's line; at mid-house a bright spirit woke; borne on a victorious wind I shed my shell like a cicada and sent a hero's cry across the northern wastes.
units.literal: I trace the dark lineage of Gaoxuan; in the mid-branch of the clan a brilliant spirit shone; through the triumphant wind I molt like a cicada, and a male voice rings across the northern wilds.

units.zh: 皇十紀而鴻漸兮，有羽儀於上京。
units.en: Ten generations later the great wild goose began its climb, and in the capital our clan spread ceremonial plumes.
units.literal: Ten reigns brought the great goose's gradual ascent; in the upper capital there were pinions and tail-feathers.

units.zh: 巨滔天而泯夏兮，考遘愍以行謠，終保己而貽則兮，里上仁之所廬。
units.en: When the flood drowned Xia, my people wandered in grief yet kept their integrity and left a pattern of life in the village they called supreme goodness.
units.literal: The vast flood covered Heaven and drowned the Xia; my forebears met sorrow and went about singing laments; in the end they kept themselves and handed down a model; in the hamlet of supreme goodness they built their hut.

units.zh: 懿前烈之純淑兮，窮與達其必濟，咨孤矇之眇眇兮，將圮絕而罔階，豈余身之足殉兮？
units.en: Their old virtue shone in every fortune, high or low; now I, a blind orphan on the edge of ruin, ask whether my life is worth the sacrifice.
units.literal: How fine the pure goodness of the former blazing deeds; whether in want or in success they were sure to aid; I consult the lonely blind child's dim sight; I am about to crumble and cut off with no stair; is it that my person is worth dying for?

units.zh: 愇世業之可懷。
units.en: I mourn because the family legacy still calls me back.
units.literal: I grieve that the inherited enterprise is worth cherishing.

units.zh: 靖潛處以永思兮，經日月而彌遠，匪黨人之敢拾兮，庶斯言之不玷。
units.en: I lie withdrawn and brood as months lengthen; no faction lifts me, yet I pray these lines stay clean.
units.literal: Quietly I lie hidden in long brooding; days and months pass ever more distant; it is not that partisans dare pick me up; I hope these words may remain unstained.

units.zh: 魂煢煢與神交兮，精誠發於宵寐，夢登山而迥眺兮，覿幽人之髣彿，㩜葛藟而授余兮，眷峻谷曰勿隧。
units.en: In dream my lonely soul meets a sage on a height; he gives me twisting vines and a voice from the gorge warns me not to bore through the cliff.
units.literal: My soul, alone, communes with the spirits; in midnight sleep earnest essence stirs; I dream I climb a mountain and gaze far off, glimpse a recluse's dim form, grasp creepers he hands me, and hear a steep valley cry, "Do not tunnel through!

units.zh: 昒昕寤而仰思兮，心蒙蒙猶未察，黃神邈而靡質兮，儀遺讖以臆對。
units.en: Dawn breaks and I am still dazed; the Yellow Spirit stays veiled, leaving only a riddle to puzzle out.
units.literal: At dawn I wake and lift my thoughts; my heart is still hazy and has not discerned; the Yellow Spirit is remote and without substance; he left a prophecy for me to answer by guess.

units.zh: 曰乘高而遌神兮，道遐通而不迷，葛綿綿於樛木兮，詠南風以為綏，蓋惴惴之臨深兮，乃二雅之所祗。
units.en: The voice said: climb high to meet the god, the path stays true, bind yourself like kudzu to a great tree, sing the southern breeze for calm, and tremble at the abyss as the Odes demand.
units.literal: It said, "You ride high and meet the god; the road, though far, does not lose the way; the kudzu spreads thick on the leaning tree; you chant the southern wind for peace; in fear and trembling you face the depth; this is what the two Ya hymns revere.

units.zh: 既誶爾以吉象兮，又申之以炯戒：盍孟晉以迨群兮？
units.en: Having shown good omens, it also warned: why not hurry on with the throng?
units.literal: Having rebuked you with auspicious images, it also repeated a blazing warning: why not press forward with the crowd?

units.zh: 辰焂忽其不再。
units.en: The moments race past and will not return.
units.literal: The hours flash by and do not come again.

units.zh: 承靈訓其虛徐兮，竚盤桓而且俟，惟天墬之無窮兮，鱻生民之脢在。
units.en: I hold the spirit's slow counsel and linger, knowing heaven and earth are endless while new generations crowd the world.
units.literal: I receive the spirit's lesson, slow and lingering; I stand turning, yet I wait; only Heaven and earth are without end; fresh are the teeming common people who dwell therein.

units.zh: 紛屯亶與蹇連兮，何艱多而智寡！
units.en: Obstacles tangle, troubles multiply, yet wisdom stays scarce.
units.literal: Tangled are obstruction and difficulty, blocked paths and hard straits; why are hardships many and wisdom few!

units.zh: 上聖寤而後拔兮，豈群黎之所御！
units.en: Only the greatest sage awakens and escapes; the mob cannot steer that fate.
units.literal: The highest sage awakens and then is lifted out; how could the mass of commoners control that!

units.zh: 昔衛叔之御昆兮，昆為寇而喪予。
units.en: Shu Wu once guarded Wei for his elder brother, yet was slain as an enemy when that brother returned.
units.literal: Formerly Shu Wu guarded Wei for his elder brother, yet was slain as an enemy when that brother returned.

units.zh: 管彎弧欲斃讎兮，讎作后而成己。
units.en: Guan Zhong drew a bow to slay his enemy, only to see that enemy become lord and finish his own rise.
units.literal: Guan bent his bow intending to kill his foe, yet the foe became ruler and completed himself.

units.zh: 變化故而相詭兮，孰云豫其終始！
units.en: Fortunes shift and mock foresight; no one reads the end from the beginning.
units.literal: Things change their grounds and deceive one another; who says you can know the end from the start!

units.zh: 雍造怨而先賞兮，丁繇惠而被戮；
units.en: Some nursed grudge yet won first reward, others earned favor yet died;
units.literal: Yong nursed resentment yet was rewarded first; Ding received favor yet was executed;

units.zh: 㮚取弔于逌吉兮，王膺慶於所慼。
units.en: Li asked for blessing from distant luck, Wang found joy in what had frightened him.
units.literal: Li sought condolence in far-off good fortune; Wang met celebration in what he had dreaded.

units.zh: 畔回宂其若茲兮，北叟頗識其倚伏。
units.en: Twists like these taught the northern elder how gain and loss lean on each other.
units.literal: Turning and returning are thus; the old man of the north somewhat knew their leaning and resting.

units.zh: 單治裏而外凋兮，張修襮而內逼，欥中龢為庶幾兮，顏與冉又不得。
units.en: Shan lost vigor though he ruled a lane, Zhang shone outward yet felt inner pinch; I aimed at the golden mean like the rare few, yet even Yan and Ran missed it.
units.literal: Shan governed the hamlet yet withered outward; Zhang spread his robe yet was pressed inward; I hoped to hit the mean like a few; yet Yan and Ran again could not attain it.

units.zh: 溺招路以從己兮，謂孔氏猶未可，安慆慆而不萉兮，卒隕身虖世禍。
units.en: Jie Ni invited Zilu to follow him, dismissing Confucius as still unworthy; Zilu would not withdraw from the world's turmoil, and in the end it cost him his life.
units.literal: Ni lured the road to follow himself and said Confucius was still not acceptable; how could he be tranquil and not weary; in the end he fell body into the age's disaster.

units.zh: 游聖門而靡救兮，顧覆醢其何補？
units.en: He haunted the Master's school yet found no rescue; when the pickle jar spilled, what good was hindsight?
units.literal: He roamed the sage's gate yet found no rescue; looking back at the overturned pickle, what could it mend?

units.zh: 固行行其必凶兮，免盜亂為賴道；
units.en: Rigid uprightness courts disaster; only shunning chaos is a trustworthy path;
units.literal: To be stubbornly upright is sure to meet ill; only avoiding robbery and chaos counts as relying on the Way;

units.zh: 形氣發于根柢兮，柯葉彙而靈茂。
units.en: Form and breath rise from the root while branches grow thick with spirit.
units.literal: form and vapor issue from the root; branches and leaves gather in numinous luxuriance.

units.zh: 恐网蜽之責景兮，慶未得其云已。
units.en: I fear the mantis scolding its shadow; good fortune has hardly begun to speak.
units.literal: I fear the mantis reproaches the shadow; the blessing is not yet done with speaking.

units.zh: 黎淳耀于高辛兮，羋彊大於南汜；
units.en: Li shone as Fire Regulator under Gaoxin, and his Mi descendants grew mighty in the south;
units.literal: Li Chun shone bright at Gaoxin; Mi grew mighty on the southern shore;

units.zh: 嬴取威於百儀兮，姜本支虖三止：既仁得其信然兮，卬天路而同軌。
units.en: Qin won awe through every ceremony, Jiang's line paused thrice at its zenith; seeing how kindness proves true, I lift my gaze to Heaven's highway and walk that track.
units.literal: Ying seized awe in the hundred rites; Jiang's root and branch halted at the third stop: having seen that benevolence is truly thus, I lift my eyes to Heaven's road and share the same track.

units.zh: 東厸虐而殲仁兮，王合位虖三五；
units.en: The eastern Yi slew kindness, yet kings aligned the threes and fives;
units.literal: Eastern Yi were cruel and slaughtered benevolence; kings united the ranks of three and five;

units.zh: 戎女烈而喪孝兮，伯徂歸於龍虎：發還師以成性兮，重醉行而自耦。
units.en: A Rong queen broke filial piety, Bo returned between dragon and tiger, disbanded troops to nurture nature, then drowned himself in wine and paired his own fetters.
units.literal: the Rong woman was fierce and destroyed filial piety; Bo departed home amid dragon and tiger; he sent the army home to perfect nature, yet again he drowned his conduct in wine and yoked himself.

units.zh: 震鱗漦于夏庭兮，匝三正而滅周；
units.en: Scales stirred in Xia's hall, turned three dynasties, and snuffed Zhou out;
units.literal: The shaking scales dripped in Xia's court; having circled the three orthodoxies it extinguished Zhou;

units.zh: 巽羽化于宣宮兮，彌五辟而成災。
units.en: Soft feathers changed in Xuan's palace and brought five reigns to ruin.
units.literal: the docile feathers transformed in Xuan's palace; spanning five rulers they completed disaster.

units.zh: 道悠長而世短兮，敻冥默而不周，胥仍物而鬼諏兮，乃窮宙而達幽。
units.en: The Way runs long while life runs short; silence never circles all; clerks still ask things of ghosts and sound the dark through time.
units.literal: The Way is long while the age is short; far and silent, it does not embrace all; the clerk still questions things and consults ghosts; then it exhausts the eon and reaches the hidden.

units.zh: 媯巢姜於孺筮兮，旦算祀于挈龜。
units.en: The Gui clan settled among the Jiang as a divination in Jingzhong's youth had foretold; the Duke of Zhou calculated his dynasty's allotted years from the tortoise shell.
units.literal: Gui dwelt among Jiang through a divination in youth; Dan counted the years by consulting the cracked tortoise shell.

units.zh: 宣、曹興敗於下夢兮，魯、衛名諡於銘謠。
units.en: Xuan and Cao rose or fell by dreams below; Lu and Wei won posthumous names from carved songs.
units.literal: Xuan and Cao rose or fell in dreams below; Lu and Wei got names and posthumous titles from inscribed songs.

units.zh: 妣聆呱而刻石兮，許相理而鞠條。
units.en: An ancestress heard a newborn wail and set it in stone; Xu read fate in twisted twigs.
units.literal: The ancestress heard the baby's wail and carved stone; Xu traced principle and bent the twigs.

units.zh: 道混成而自然兮，術同原而分流。
units.en: The Way blends whole and follows nature; methods spring from one root yet branch apart.
units.literal: The Way blends into completion and follows nature; arts share one source yet divide in flow.

units.zh: 神先心以定命兮，命隨行以消息。
units.en: Spirit settles fate before the heart knows it; fate then rides every deed up or down.
units.literal: The spirit precedes the heart to fix fate; fate follows conduct to wax and wane.

units.zh: 斡流遷其不濟兮，故遭罹而贏縮。
units.en: The turning stream never rests; fortune therefore tightens and slackens with each blow.
units.literal: The pivoting current shifts and does not ford; therefore one meets disaster and tightens or slackens.

units.zh: 三欒同於一體兮，雖移盈然不忒。
units.en: Three luan share one frame; though plenty shifts, the rule holds true.
units.literal: The three stems share one body; though fullness moves, it is not wrong.

units.zh: 洞參差其紛錯兮，斯眾兆之所惑。
units.en: Deeply tangled omens bewilder the common crowd.
units.literal: Profoundly uneven, tangled and confused: these are the many omens by which the multitude is deluded.

units.zh: 周、賈盪而貢憤兮，齊死生與禍福，抗爽言以矯情兮，信畏犧而忌服。
units.en: Zhuang Zhou and Jia Yi railed in reckless essays, treating life and death, fortune and woe, as one; their brave words chided human passion, yet they still shrank from the butchered ox and hated the halter.
units.literal: Zhou and Jia swung wide and poured forth indignant feeling; they equated death with life and disaster with blessing; they set bold words against passion; they truly feared the sacrificial ox yet dreaded bondage.

units.zh: 所貴聖人之至論兮，順天性而斷誼。
units.en: The highest teaching is the sage's verdict: trust innate nature and judge duty accordingly.
units.literal: What is honored is the sage's ultimate teaching: follow Heaven's nature and decide what is right.

units.zh: 物有欲而不居兮，亦有惡而不避，守孔約而不貳兮，乃輶德而無累。
units.en: You may crave yet not clutch, shrink from evil yet not dodge duty; hold fast to the Master's spare rule and virtue rides easy.
units.literal: Things may attract desire yet one does not cling; there are loathings one does not flee; keep Confucius's restraint undivided—then you steer virtue lightly and bear no burden.

units.zh: 三仁殊而一致兮，夷、惠舛而齊聲。
units.en: The three benevolent worthies walked different paths to the same goal; Yi and Hui clashed in style yet harmonized in purpose.
units.literal: The three benevolent men differed yet aimed at one end; Bo Yi and Hui differed in conduct yet shared one voice.

units.zh: 木偃息以蕃魏兮，申重繭以存荊。
units.en: Duan Ganmu's retirement by moral example strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu's bleeding feet saved Chu from ruin.
units.literal: Duan Ganmu rested in withdrawal and thereby strengthened Wei; Shen Baoxu wore through layer upon layer of calluses and thereby preserved Chu.

units.zh: 紀焚躬以衛上兮，皓頤志而弗營。
units.en: Ji Xin gave his body for the emperor; the Four Elders fed their resolve and shunned ambition.
units.literal: Ji burned his body to shield his lord; the Four Hoary Ones nourished their will and sought no gain.

units.zh: 侯屮木之區別兮，苟能實而必榮。
units.en: Trees and shrubs differ, yet any that bears true fruit will thrive.
units.literal: Observe how tree and shrub are not the same: if they can bear fruit they will surely flourish.

units.zh: 要沒世而不朽兮，乃先民之所程。
units.en: To perish yet leave an undying name is the standard the ancients strove for.
units.literal: To die yet not decay—this is the measure the ancient people set.

units.zh: 觀天罔之紘覆兮，實棐諶而相順，謨先聖之大繇兮，亦厸德而助信。
units.en: Heaven's canopy rewards sincerity; the sages' great paths gather lesser goodness into faith.
units.literal: I gaze on the vast net Heaven stretches as cover: it truly supports good faith and brings things into accord; I trace the great tracks charted by former sages: they also gather nearby virtue and strengthen trust.

units.zh: 虞韶美而儀鳳兮，孔忘味於千載。
units.en: The Shao dance of Emperor Shun so moved nature that phoenixes flocked; Confucius forgot his meal for ages after hearing it.
units.literal: Shun's shao music was beautiful and phoenixes danced in measure; Confucius forgot flavor for a thousand years.

units.zh: 素文信而底麟兮，漢賓祚于異代。
units.en: The uncrowned king's classic drew the qilin at the end; Han inherited that mandate in a later era.
units.literal: The uncrowned king's plain script proved trustworthy and a unicorn appeared at the end; Han receives its blessing in another age.

units.zh: 精通靈而感物兮，神動氣而入微。
units.en: When essence meets spirit it moves the world; spirit rides breath into the finest grain of things.
units.literal: Essence penetrates the numinous and stirs things; spirit moves vapor and enters the subtle.

units.zh: 養游睇而猿號兮，李虎發而石開。
units.en: Prince Yang's wandering glance made gibbons wail; Li Guang's tiger shot cracked the boulder.
units.literal: Yang roamed and gazed, and apes cried out; Li Guang drew his bow as a tiger and split the stone.

units.zh: 非精誠其焉通兮，苟無實其孰信！
units.en: Without utter sincerity nothing connects; without inward truth no one trusts the sign.
units.literal: Were it not for utmost sincerity, how could it penetrate? If there were no inner truth, who would believe?

units.zh: 操末技猶必然兮，矧湛躬於道真！
units.en: Trifling arts demand truth at last; how much more the man who drowns himself in the genuine Way.
units.literal: Even petty skills, when pursued, have their necessity; how much more when you steep your person in the true Way!

units.zh: 登孔、顥而上下兮，緯群龍之所經，朝貞觀而夕化兮，猶諠己而遺形，若胤彭而偕老兮，訴來哲以通情。
units.en: Climb the heights of Confucius and Yan Hui, follow the dragons' tracks, wake to the true pattern by dusk though ego still chatters, shed the shell, and if you walk with Peng Zu into age, leave a thread of feeling for sages yet unborn.
units.literal: Ascend Confucius and Yan Hui, roam up and down; trace the paths all dragons have traveled; in the morning behold the correct model and by evening transform; though the clamor of self remains, cast off the form; if you follow Peng and grow old together, tell later wise men to convey the feeling.

units.zh: 亂曰：天造屮昧，立性命兮，復心弘道，惟賢聖兮。
units.en: Coda: Heaven began in twilight and fixed our natures; broadening the mind and the Way is work for sages alone.
units.literal: Envoi: Heaven in the beginning created darkness and set life and nature; restore the mind and enlarge the Way—only the worthy and sage can do it.

units.zh: 渾元運物，流不處兮，
units.en: The cosmic breath rolls creation onward and never lingers in one place.
units.literal: The primal vapor moves things and never rests in one place;

units.zh: 保身遺名，民之表兮。
units.en: Keep the body whole yet leave a name: that is the people's pattern.
units.literal: Preserve the person and leave a name—that is the people's model.

units.zh: 舍生取誼，亦道用兮，憂傷夭物，忝莫痛兮！
units.en: To die for duty is also the Way's tool; to wound creation through worry is the bitterest disgrace.
units.literal: Cast away life to take rightness—this too is the Way's use; to fret and harm Heaven's creatures—there is no shame more bitter!

units.zh: 昊爾太素，
units.en: O boundless primal simplicity,
units.literal: Vast, you primal plainness,

units.zh: 曷渝色兮？
units.en: why should you shift your color?
units.literal: why change your hue?

units.zh: 尚粵其幾，淪神域兮！
units.en: I would rise on your hidden hinge and plunge into the spirit's domain.
units.literal: I would mount your subtle pivot and sink into the spirit's realm!

units.zh: 永平中為郎，典校祕書，專篤志於博學，以著述為業。
units.en: Under Yongping he entered as a court gentleman, supervised collation of the palace library, gave himself wholly to learning, and took writing for his life's work.
units.literal: In the Yongping years he became a gentleman-attendant, collated the secretariat books, devoted himself single-mindedly to wide learning, and made authorship his occupation.

units.zh: 或譏以無功，又感東方朔、揚雄自諭以不遭蘇、張、范、蔡之時，曾不折之以正道，明君子之所守，故聊復應焉。
units.en: Critics mocked his want of deeds; remembering how Dongfang Shuo and Yang Xiong excused their obscurity by the absence of Su or Zhang, yet never rebuked opportunism with the true Way, he felt compelled to answer.
units.literal: Some ridiculed him for lacking achievement; he was also moved that Dongfang Shuo and Yang Xiong, explaining themselves as having missed the age of Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Fan Ju, and Cai Ze, had not refuted this with the correct Way or clarified what the gentleman guards; therefore he briefly answered in turn.

units.zh: 其辭曰：
units.en: The piece opens:
units.literal: Its words say:

units.zh: 賓戲主人曰：「蓋聞聖人有壹定之論，列士有不易之分，亦云名而已矣。
units.en: The guest said to the host, "Sages hold one steady teaching, steadfast men one fixed portion, and fame is said to crown the whole affair.
units.literal: The guest teased the host, saying, "I have heard that sages have one settled doctrine and knights-errant an unchanging lot; they also say it comes down to name alone.

units.zh: 故太上有立德，其次有立功。
units.en: The highest goal is founding imperishable virtue; next comes founding merit.
units.literal: Therefore the highest is to establish virtue; next is to establish merit.

units.zh: 夫德不得後身而特盛，功不得背時而獨章，是以聖喆之治，棲棲皇皇，孔席不煗，墨突不黔。
units.en: Virtue cannot peak if you put yourself last, nor can merit blaze if you ignore the hour; hence true sages never rest—Confucius' mat stayed cool, Mozi's hearth stayed clean.
units.literal: Virtue cannot flourish if it comes only after the self; merit cannot shine if it turns its back on the times; therefore the ordering of the wise and good is restless and hurried—Confucius' mat never grew warm, Mozi's chimney never blackened.

units.zh: 由此言之，取舍者昔人之上務，著作者前列之餘事耳。
units.en: Choosing a path was the ancients' first duty; composing books came after.
units.literal: From this it follows that choosing what to embrace was the ancients' chief task, while setting brush to paper ranked as a leftover among lesser priorities.

units.zh: 今吾子幸游帝王之世，躬帶冕之服，浮英華，湛道德，矕龍虎之文，舊矣。
